title: Noetherianity and local regularity of strict hensel divisor quotient
statement: Let R be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], f in R, and assume R/(f) is regular. Let Ω be an algebraically closed field and barY : Spec Ω → Spec R a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let b : R → strictHenselizationRing barY [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] induce the canonical structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] on spectra, and assume b(f) is not a unit. Then strictHenselizationRing barY/(b(f)) is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and its localization at every prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local. The canonically isomorphic full affine-neighbourhood colimit has the same properties.

proof.text: Apply the algebraic divisor-quotient presentation to the full affine-neighbourhood strict henselization, its structural ring map b, and the nonunit b(f). Obtain a prime p of R/(f), its residue-field separable closure K, and the strict-henselization structure on the divisor quotient over the prime localization.

Since R/(f) is regular, Mathlib gives regular locality and Noetherianity of its prime localization A. Apply Algebra.isRegularLocalRing_iff_strictHenselization to this A, K, and the actual divisor quotient to obtain its regular locality.

A regular local ring is Noetherian by its class fields. For each prime q of the quotient apply IsRegularLocalRing.localization_at_prime_and_isRegularRing to obtain its regular prime localization. Combine these two clauses.

theorem strictHenselizationRing_divisor_quotient_noetherian_and_local_regular
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (f : R)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselization barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictLocalizationToBase barY)
    (hg : ¬ IsUnit (b.hom f)) :
    IsNoetherianRing (strictHenselization barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}) ∧
      ∀ (p : Ideal (strictHenselization barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}))
        [p.IsPrime],
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)

statement_change.old_statement: The strict henselization divisor quotient is Noetherian and all its prime localizations are regular local.
statement_change.what: Make the contextual statement self-contained by spelling out the hypotheses formerly supplied by its parent. Replace the parent-theorem statement dependency with the definitions used in the statement; the parent proof uses this auxiliary, so retaining that contextual edge would introduce a false dependency cycle. The small and full colimit formulations are related by the canonical ring isomorphism, as explicitly proved in the consumer. Mathematical content is unchanged.

old_proof.text: Use the canonical small-to-full affine-colimit ring isomorphism e. Its coprojection formula identifies Spec(e.hom) followed by the small structural map with strictLocalizationToBase. Transport b along e.hom; an inverse map proves that its image of f is still a nonunit. Apply the retained upstream divisor-quotient presentation. The inverse ring equivalence sends the principal ideal generated by (b followed by e.hom)(f) to the ideal generated by b(f), so Ideal.quotientEquiv gives the quotient ring isomorphism. Pull the supplied local-base algebra action back through this isomorphism, and compose the pointed-etale universal cocone isomorphism with the resulting algebra isomorphism. This gives the same algebraic strict henselization property on the original small-colimit divisor quotient, without using regularity.
